title: I Tried 6 Vegan Egg Substitutes For Baking Cupcakes
summary: In this Goodful video, Merle explores six vegan egg substitutes by baking cupcakes from a vegan yellow cake mix to keep variables consistent. She tests aquafaba, carbonated water, applesauce, mashed banana, flax egg, and a water–oil–baking powder slurry, comparing texture, binding, and flavor. Through bake-and-taste rounds, she scores each substitute, notes failures (notably with aquafaba and certain slurry blends), and crowns flax egg as the winner for its binding, light texture, and neutral flavor. The evaluation highlights that vegan substitutions don’t always behave like real eggs in standard cake mixes and offers practical takeaways for home bakers.
topics: taste-testing and scoring in food experiments

sections.title: Introduction, test plan, and initial batter prep
concepts: vegan yellow cake mix as standardized base
sections.description: Merle introduces the goal of testing six vegan egg substitutes for cupcakes, inspired by a Kitchen article. To control variables, she uses a vegan yellow cake mix as the base and divides batter into portions, acknowledging a minor measurement hiccup (thirds vs full cups) while preparing the first batch.

sections.title: Batch 1: aquafaba, carbonated water, and additional base substitutions
sections.description: First batch is prepared with aquafaba and water, plus carbonated water considered with skepticism. Merle pours batter into muffin tins and bakes the initial set, then prepares for the next substitutions in batch two.

sections.title: Batch 2: banana, applesauce, flax egg, and tasting phase
sections.description: Batch two covers mashed banana, applesauce, a flax egg (prepared with flax and water and allowed to thicken), and notes on the binding and texture across substitutes. After baking, Merle tastes each cupcake, comments on flavor implications (notably banana presence), and assigns scores, culminating in the flax egg as the standout.

sections.title: Conclusion, winner, and practical takeaways
concepts: viewer prompts for more vegan testing
sections.description: Merle concludes that the flax egg is the winner for its binding, texture, and flavor, while acknowledging that the Kitchen article’s top-rated substitutes (carbonated water and oil–water–baking powder) did not perform as well in this test. She emphasizes that not all substitutions work well in every vegan baking scenario and invites viewer input for future tests.
